description: For a page that runs no JavaScript (a static page that shares a component with the app): the file as plain CSS. A rule per state under a selector the page toggles (or :hover, :active and :focus when the file enters the state on hover, press or focus), transitions carrying each motion (springs as linear()), the way in on mount from @starting-style, colors in oklab(). Checked against nudg's runtime at 60 points and two sizes; differences and what the page loses without a script (drags, timers, kicks, loops, layout from another element) are listed. Don't add a script to a static page yourself: tell the person what it loses and let them decide; when they want it exact, pass script: true for a module that plays the file on nudg's runtime. Ask the person which class or attribute stands for each state when the page has one.

file.description: Path to a .nudg.json file, relative to the working directory.

mount.description: The event the element is shown with as it mounts, e.g. host.show: its way in plays from @starting-style.

path.description: With `source`: where the text would live, for resolving imports and labeling.

rev.description: With `file`: read it as it was at this git revision (HEAD, HEAD~1, a branch) instead of from disk, imports included.

script.description: Also return a script (an ES module) that plays the file on nudg's runtime, exactly, where the page runs JavaScript; the CSS stays the fallback. Only when the person decided the page may load JavaScript.

scriptSrc.description: With script: the URL of a copy of nudg's dist folder the site serves itself, instead of jsDelivr.

source.description: The file's JSON text, to check before writing it. Imports resolve relative to `path`, or the working directory.

states.description: A selector per state that matches while it is active, e.g. { "hidden": "[data-closing]" }. Default [data-nudg-state~="<name>"].

targets.description: A selector per target, e.g. { "menu": ".lnb" }. Default [data-nudg="<name>"].

name: nudg_to_css
title: A nudg file as plain CSS
